title: Weaning piglets: age, timing, and transition
subtitle: Getting piglets onto solid feed and sow back to condition.
excerpt: Weaning is the point when piglets are separated from the sow and the sow's milk supply ceases. The right age to wean depends on piglet development, the sow's condition, and your management system. In the UK, piglets must not be weaned before 28 days of age. Most smallholding litters are weaned at 5 to 8 weeks.
sourceNotes: DEFRA Code of Practice for the Welfare of Pigs (2003), weaning section. AHDB Pork, Piglet Nutrition at Weaning factsheet (2018). Andy Case, Outdoor Pig Production (Crowood Press, 2008), chapter on growing pigs.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temporary growth check that occurs in piglets immediately after weaning as they adjust to a solid diet and cope with the stress of separation.
A highly digestible starter feed introduced to piglets from about 10 to 14 days of age alongside milk, to prepare the gut for weaning.

content.text: Weaning is a transition for both the piglets and the sow. Piglets need to be eating solid feed before the milk supply disappears, and the sow needs to regain body condition before being re-mated. Getting the timing right reduces the post-weaning growth check and returns the sow to oestrus quickly.

Piglets must not be weaned before 28 days of age under the Welfare of Farmed Animals (England) Regulations 2007. Weaning before 21 days is not permitted under any circumstances. Most smallholding producers wean at 5 to 8 weeks and this is where the welfare outcomes are best.

Remove the sow from the litter, not the piglets from the sow's housing. This keeps the piglets in familiar surroundings and reduces their stress. The sow moves to a separate recovery pen.

Keep the litter together for the first week post-weaning. Separating littermates adds competition and further stress. Merging litters from different sows at weaning often leads to fighting; if you must mix, do so at night with a distracting feed.
Maintain the weaner creep at 30 to 32 C for the first week if weaning before 5 weeks of age. Older piglets are less temperature-sensitive.

The sow's milk supply dries up within 2 to 3 days of weaning. She may be uncomfortable and restless during this period. Check her udder daily for signs of mastitis: heat, hardness, or red discolouration in any one quarter. Reduce her feed slightly for 2 days post-weaning to help dry her off, then return her to full ration.

Most sows return to oestrus 4 to 7 days after weaning. If you want a short weaning-to-service interval, score her condition at weaning: a sow below BCS 2.5 needs 2 to 3 weeks to recover before re-mating for best results.

attrs.cue: Weaners not eating solid feed in the first 48 hours
attrs.cause: Unfamiliar feed, or piglets were not offered creep before weaning
attrs.fix: Offer a little fresh feed three times daily in small amounts rather than a full hopper. Dampen the feed slightly. If they still refuse after 72 hours, ask the vet for advice on syringe-feeding a piglet-specific liquid feed.

attrs.cue: Sow has not returned to oestrus by 3 weeks post-weaning
attrs.cause: Poor body condition (under BCS 2.5), heavy lactation drain, or low light levels in winter
attrs.fix: Check body condition score and increase feed if below 2.5. Ensure the sow gets boar contact, even through a fence — the boar's presence stimulates oestrus.
